// diagnostic

L0510

Declaration replaces a readable Core prelude alias (D-NAME-ALIAS1)

What

Declaration replaces a readable Core prelude alias (D-NAME-ALIAS1)

Why

User declarations win over the compiler-opened alias, but the replacement is worth seeing

Fix

Keep the declaration, or rename it to use the prelude alias

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning L0510: tests/ui_lint/prelude_shadow_warn.warn.

Warning [L0510] (prelude_alias_shadow): declaration print replaces a Core prelude alias
  --> tests/ui_lint/prelude_shadow_warn.jet:1:4
    |
  1 | fn print() {}
    |    ^^^^^
 Why: the readable Core prelude opens this name automatically, and a user declaration wins in its file
 Fix: keep the declaration to accept the shadow, or rename it to use the prelude alias
More: jet-lang.dev/e/L0510

Warning [L0104] (unused_private_fn): private function `print` is never called or used as a value.
  --> tests/ui_lint/prelude_shadow_warn.jet:1:4
    |
  1 | fn print() {}
    |    ^^^^^
 Why: a private function with no reachable reference is dead code; public functions stay exempt because other modules may use them.
 Fix: remove the function, or rename `print` to `_print` when it is intentional.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/L0104
